absent: Full layouts of device and link and firmware node and firmware handle and ACPI device and event environment and attribute group and power operations and power message beyond referenced members.
Implementations of generic search routines for bus and class and driver including locking and reference counting and traversal order.
Implementations of plural group add and remove routines and of name and firmware and device number and any and ACPI matchers.
Lock ordering among device mutex and bus and class and driver locks plus sleep versus atomic context for all callbacks.
Behavior of internal lock class setter and lockdep matching and novalidate setter and one time warning beyond the call sites.

Implementations of root registration and node aware resource allocation and base managed allocators and reallocators and duplicators and per CPU allocator and action handling and string attribute reader.
Semantics and error handling for probe and sync and remove and shutdown and online and offline and suspend and resume and coredump and DMA setup and teardown.
Uevent generation and sysfs visibility and namespace type handling and ownership assignment and node naming details.
Device control enforcement when enabled including direct permission logic and whiteout device definition and major minor decoding choice between internal and user views.
Signature key and MPI encoding and keyring handling and timestamp use and verification when supported.
Moderation tuning algorithm and profile selection and state transitions and reclamation protocol beyond the helpers.
NUMA policy and allocation flag meanings and size helper implementations and per CPU lifetime rules.
Module alias consumption and loadable versus built in registration ordering and initcall sequencing.
Faux device creation and registration and probe and remove invocation context and driver data lifetime.
Numeric values and stability guarantees for bus notification and probe strategy and key algorithm and digest algorithm enumerators.

findings.text: Two build variants assign a custom lock class to a device mutex. The checking variant warns once when replacing an existing custom class and otherwise delegates to the internal setter with a stringified key name plus the key object. The plain variant always delegates directly with the same two key representations.
Reset helper restores the device mutex to a non validating lock class using the mutex dependency map, a fixed descriptive name and the current program position.

Firmware node accessor returns null when firmware support is disabled or the device pointer is missing, otherwise it returns the associated node. Virtual function count returns zero when the bus or its counting operation is absent, otherwise it returns the bus operation result for the device.
Root device registration macro forwards its name argument to the internal root registration routine together with the current module owner.
Platform data accessor returns the platform data pointer stored in the device object for read only callers.
Single group helpers wrap the plural group routines by building a two element list holding the given group followed by termination, then adding or removing that list for the device.
Device filesystem mount helper in this configuration always reports success without performing work.
Link flag test reports whether any of the requested flag bits are present in the link flag set, normalizing the result to a boolean.
Character device alias macros generate module alias strings for a fixed major and minor pair and for a fixed major with any minor, using string conversion of the numeric arguments.

Bus descriptor carries name plus dev name plus three group tables for bus and device and driver. Matching uses match while event reporting uses uevent. Lifecycle uses probe and sync state and remove and shutdown. Further operations cover affinity query and online and offline and suspend and resume and virtual function counting and DMA setup and teardown. Power handling uses pm while override behavior and parent lock need use dedicated booleans.

Bus attribute record pairs a generic attribute with read handling and write handling for a bus using buffers with length on writes. Read handling corresponds to show while write handling corresponds to store. Companion helpers declare instances with read write access or read only access or write only access.

Bus search uses two callback types. Matching takes a device plus opaque comparison data and returns an integer verdict. Iteration takes a device plus mutable caller data and returns an integer control code.

Bus lookup helpers delegate to a generic bus search with a fixed matcher. Name lookup starts from a given device and matches by name. Firmware node and firmware handle and device number lookups start from the beginning with their respective matchers. Next device lookup resumes from a current device using a matcher that accepts any entry.

ACPI based bus lookup has two configurations. When ACPI matching is available it delegates to generic search with the ACPI matcher from the start. When unavailable it always returns null without searching.

Bus notification enumerates device and driver lifecycle stages. Device stages cover addition and deletion request and completed removal. Driver stages cover bind attempt and successful bind and unbind attempt and completed unbind, plus a distinct stage for a driver that did not bind.

Class descriptor carries a name plus group tables for class and device. It provides event reporting and node naming plus release handlers for class and device plus a pre shutdown hook. Namespace handling uses type operations and a lookup plus ownership assignment. Power handling uses a dedicated operations pointer. Iteration state pairs a list iterator with an optional device type filter and private subsystem data.
Class lookup helpers delegate to generic class search with fixed matchers from the start. Variants match by name or by firmware node or by firmware handle or by device number respectively.
ACPI based class lookup delegates with the ACPI matcher when available, otherwise it always returns null without searching and accepts an opaque pointer in place of an ACPI object.

Class attribute record pairs a generic attribute with read and write handlers operating on a class and attribute with buffers. Companion helpers declare read write or read only or write only instances. String variant extends the record with a character pointer. String construction helpers bind a fixed read routine with no write routine for a given name and mode and string.
Class file helpers forward to namespace aware file routines with an empty namespace, creating with a must check status or removing without a result.
Class interface record links into a list and points to its class, with callbacks invoked on device addition returning a status and on device removal without a result.

Managed resource callbacks separate cleanup from comparison. Release takes a device plus resource pointer without returning. Matching takes a device plus resource plus comparison data and returns an integer verdict.

Resource allocation macros forward to a node aware allocator with release routine and size and allocation flags plus a stringified release name, using no NUMA preference by default or an explicit node when requested.

Managed zeroing allocation adds zeroing to the base managed allocator. Array helpers validate element count multiplication and return null on overflow, otherwise allocating the computed byte total with or without zeroing for the calloc form.
Managed array reallocation validates new count multiplication and returns null on overflow, otherwise forwarding the computed byte total to the base managed reallocator with the given flags.
Managed array duplication computes the total size from element size and count via a size product helper, then duplicates the source buffer with the given flags.
Managed per CPU allocation macro forwards to the generic managed per CPU allocator with the size and alignment of the requested type, casting the result to a typed per CPU pointer.
Three mapping helpers in this configuration always fail with an encoded I O error pointer for invalid arguments. The error encoding macro converts a negative errno into a typed I O error pointer.
Managed action removal forwards to a quiet removal routine and warns when that routine reports failure.

Action registration macro records a callback with data plus a stringified action name. The reset variant attempts registration and on failure immediately executes the callback with its data before returning the failure status. A companion macro supplies the stringified name automatically.
Probe strategy enumeration distinguishes default handling from a preference for asynchronous probing and from forced synchronous probing.

Driver descriptor carries a name plus bus link plus module owner plus built in name. It controls sysfs bind attributes and probe strategy plus firmware match tables. Lifecycle uses probe and state sync and remove and shutdown plus suspend and resume plus group tables plus power operations plus coredump. Private data uses a dedicated pointer while a nested record holds a Rust only post unbind hook invoked after removal but before resource release.
Driver attribute record pairs a generic attribute with read and write handlers operating on a driver with buffers. Companion helpers declare read write or read only or write only instances.

Driver lookup helpers delegate to generic driver search with fixed matchers. Name and firmware node and firmware handle and device number variants start from the beginning, while next device lookup resumes from a given start using an accept any matcher.
ACPI based driver lookup delegates with the ACPI matcher when available, otherwise it always returns null without searching and accepts an opaque pointer in place of an ACPI object.

Driver registration helpers generate module lifecycle routines. The loadable form creates an init routine that registers the driver with extra arguments and an exit routine that unregisters it. The built in form creates only an init routine hooked into device init processing.

Faux device wraps a generic device as its sole member with a conversion helper that recovers the container from the embedded member. Its operations record carries probe returning a status plus remove without a result, both operating on the faux container.
Faux driver data accessors delegate to generic driver data routines on the embedded device, retrieving a pointer or storing a given pointer.

Access value DEVCG_ACC_MKNOD is one and DEVCG_ACC_READ is two and DEVCG_ACC_WRITE is four with DEVCG_ACC_MASK combining all three. Type value DEVCG_DEV_BLOCK is one and DEVCG_DEV_CHAR is two and DEVCG_DEV_ALL is four meaning every device.

Permission check allows files that are neither block nor character and allows entries with no device number. It maps block versus character kinds and translates write and read request bits into control access bits, then delegates to a type and major and minor check.

Node creation check allows modes that are neither block nor character and allows a whiteout character case. It maps character versus block kinds and requests mknod access for the decoded major and minor pair.

Internal number decoding shifts right by the minor bit width to obtain major and masks with the minor mask to obtain minor. User API decoding shifts right by eight for major and keeps the low eight bits for minor.
Fallback permission routines always allow. The direct type check and the inode permission and node creation variants in the disabled configuration report success without inspecting arguments.

Key algorithm set holds RSA plus a maximum sentinel while digest set holds SHA1 plus SHA256 plus a maximum. Public key header carries version plus timestamp plus algorithm plus MPI count plus a trailing MPI area and is packed. Signature header adds hash identifier plus an eight byte key identifier with the same trailing area and packing.
Signature verification stub in this configuration always reports operation not supported without inspecting its keyring or signature or digest arguments.

Moderation profile count NET_DIM_PARAMS_NUM_PROFILES is five with default RX packets NET_DIM_DEFAULT_RX_CQ_PKTS_FROM_EQE is two hundred fifty six and default TX packets NET_DIM_DEFAULT_TX_CQ_PKTS_FROM_EQE is one hundred twenty eight. Default profile selectors for CQE and EQE are each one. Event count DIM_NEVENTS is sixty four.

Significance test requires a non zero reference and reports true when relative deviation exceeds ten percent. Gap helper computes forward distance between start and end modulo two raised to the given bit width.
Moderation record holds microsecond delay plus packet threshold plus completion threshold plus a period mode byte, with a deferred reclamation header for safe updates.
Profile capability DIM_PROFILE_RX is bit zero and DIM_PROFILE_TX is bit one. Coalesce capabilities are DIM_COALESCE_USEC bit zero and DIM_COALESCE_PKTS bit one and DIM_COALESCE_COMPS bit two.

Callers must handle null on array size overflow and error pointers from mapping stubs and always fail status from signature verification. Removal warns on failure while registration with reset executes the callback on failure. Lock class replacement warns when overriding a custom class. Permissive fallbacks silently allow device control and mount operations.
Header guards define unique inclusion markers that prevent repeated processing of bus and class and resource and driver and faux and signature and moderation headers.
External dependency used when validating managed array sizes.
External dependency used when computing managed duplication sizes.
External dependency used when decoding device majors for permission checks.
External dependency used when decoding device minors for permission checks.
